prompts.terrain:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production pixel-art terrain tile atlas for the top-down 2D game Last Tram, a contemporary European old-town district.
Primary request: A precisely ordered 4-column by 4-row sprite tile atlas, square 1024 by 1024 pixels, exactly 16 rectangular tiles and nothing else. Each tile fills its entire 256 by 256 pixel cell, edge-to-edge, with NO margins, NO gutters, NO divider lines, NO labels, NO text. Tile seams exactly at x=256,512,768 and y=256,512,768.
Style/medium: authentic restrained 16-bit pixel art. Each tile depicts a 16 by 16 logical pixel tile enlarged 16x using nearest-neighbor, with visibly large square pixel clusters, crisp hard edges, a limited shared palette and zero antialiasing. Avoid high-resolution details. Orthographic overhead view, north at top, zero isometric perspective. Cozy urban dusk ambience; brown oak, cream stone, muted blue-grey pavements, dark slate asphalt, natural sage greens, teal canal water. Flat even lighting, no cast shadows across tile edges. These are game-ready repeatable textures, not an illustration.
Exact row-major tile order:
Row 1: (1) horizontal honey-brown oak floorboards; (2) cream indoor square ceramic floor tiles; (3) grey-beige church stone floor slabs; (4) cool grey sidewalk square paving slabs.
Row 2: (1) uneven muted taupe old-town cobblestones; (2) plain dark blue-grey asphalt road with sparse wear, no lane marking; (3) east-west tram rail tile, two parallel horizontal steel rails inset in dark asphalt, rails continue perfectly left to right; (4) pedestrian zebra crossing on asphalt, a set of narrow cream stripes oriented vertically so a pedestrian walks north-south.
Row 3: (1) muted green park grass; (2) dense clipped dark green hedge texture, repeating without a border; (3) calm teal canal water with sparse small pixel ripples, no shore; (4) light worn stone bridge deck texture, repeating, no railing or water.
Row 4: (1) north-south tram rail tile, two parallel vertical steel rails in asphalt continue top to bottom; (2) asphalt road variant with a small worn cream center-line dash horizontal at its vertical center; (3) teal canal water alternate ripple frame; (4) cobblestone alternate variation without litter.
Constraints: exactly four rows of four equally sized tiles; repeatable textures; no objects, no furniture, no people, no scenery, no letters, no watermark, no rendered checkerboard. Opaque backgrounds throughout. Pixel art on a strict chunky square grid.
prompts.architecture:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent pixel-art wall and doorway tile atlas for Last Tram, a contemporary European old-town top-down game with 16-pixel map cells.
Primary request: ONE square PNG 1024x1024, a precisely regular 4 columns x 4 rows atlas. Each sprite is confined to one 256x256 slot. No gutter, no labels, no visible grid. The background must be genuinely transparent alpha. Each slot's artwork is logically a 16x16 pixel tile enlarged 16x, with chunky hard square pixels, few colors, no tiny texture speckles, no antialiasing, no perspective.
Style: orthographic straight overhead; simple 16-bit pixel game art, aged warm beige masonry with a dark umber outline, pale stone cap highlights, modest desaturated teal window glass, oak doors, subtle warm interior light. The wall strips have consistent thickness: approximately 5 of the 16 logical pixels, and extend exactly to the relevant cell edges. Transparency on either side of wall strips. These are adjoining pieces of the same top-down cutaway wall, not freestanding buildings, not front-facing wall facades.
EXACT left-to-right row order:
Row 1: straight east-west wall strip through middle of tile; straight north-south wall strip through middle; L corner connecting EAST and SOUTH; L corner connecting WEST and SOUTH.
Row 2: L corner connecting EAST and NORTH; L corner connecting WEST and NORTH; T junction connecting WEST,EAST,SOUTH; T junction connecting WEST,EAST,NORTH.
Row 3: T junction connecting NORTH,SOUTH,EAST; T junction connecting NORTH,SOUTH,WEST; + junction connecting all four sides; isolated square masonry pillar in center with transparent surround.
Row 4: east-west wall strip interrupted by a closed teal glass window; north-south wall strip interrupted by matching teal glass window; east-west wall strip interrupted by closed warm oak door; north-south wall strip interrupted by matching closed oak door.
Constraints: Exactly 16 tile sprites, exactly four in each row. All connected wall ends reach the cell edges for tiling. No cast ground shadows, no floor texture, no grass, no checkerboard painted into transparency, no labels, no lettering, no characters, no watermark. Sharp coarse pixel art.
prompts.small_props:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent pixel-art single-cell object sprite atlas for the top-down European old-town game Last Tram.
Primary request: A square sprite sheet, exactly 4 columns and 4 rows with 16 DIFFERENT isolated sprites. All 16 cell backgrounds are genuine alpha transparency, no painted checkerboard. Equal-size cells. No labels or drawn grid.
Style/medium: coarse authentic 16-bit RPG pixel art. Each cell represents ONE 16x16 logical-pixel map cell enlarged for display. Draw each object with a small number of large square pixel clusters, a limited palette, dark brown outlines, crisp unaliased edges, and NO fine grain. Shallow overhead orthographic RPG view, object tops visible and a small south-facing front visible. Everything faces DOWN/SOUTH. Warm beige/ivory appliances, teal glass, dark blue-grey metal, honey oak wood, muted rust accents. Same lighting from upper left. All sprites remain inside their cells with generous transparent space; no cast floor shadows or floor patches.
EXACT left-to-right order:
Row 1: ivory kitchen refrigerator with freezer split and dark handle; compact dark-grey four-burner kitchen stove with small oven front; square white tiled shower tray with blue glass partition and silver shower fitting; compact cream sink basin and silver faucet.
Row 2: small dark television on a low stand, blue-black screen; oak desk with one OPEN dark laptop; small round café table with one coffee cup; blue-grey ATM machine with teal display, slot and small keypad.
Row 3: narrow glass tram timetable display case on a small metal upright; church service bulletin board of dark wood with a few cream paper slips; old simple wooden vestry chair with tan seat; oak wardrobe with two doors.
Row 4: dark charcoal reclining barber chair with armrests and chrome pedestal; ivory front-loading washing machine with round teal window; slim dark cast-iron street lamp with one warm amber lantern (keep whole lamp inside one cell); compact stone stair tile with a clear set of six grey-beige steps ascending north.
Constraints: Exactly 16 sprites, four per row, clean alpha transparency; no humans, no extra sprites, no background environment, no ground platforms, no labels, no readable text, no branding, no watermark. Sprite shapes unmistakably readable at small game scale.
prompts.furniture:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent pixel-art furniture and park prop sprite atlas for Last Tram, a top-down contemporary European old-town game.
Primary request: ONE square sprite sheet, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 isolated sprites in exactly the order below. Genuine transparent alpha across all empty space. Uniform empty slots, no labels, no painted checkerboard, no visible cell lines.
Style/medium: authentic coarse 16-bit RPG pixel art; hard square pixel clusters, dark brown outline, restrained shared palette of honey oak, warm cream, muted brick-red fabric, blue-grey metal, teal water, olive green leaves. Shallow overhead orthographic RPG camera, object top clearly visible, a small south-facing front visible. No isometric angle. Pixel art, no high resolution fine-detail illustration. Even top-left lighting; minimal object shading and no floor patches or ground-plane shadows.
The base game tile is 16 logical pixels. Furniture footprints below MUST read with the stated proportions: 2x1 objects are TWICE AS WIDE AS TALL, beds and fountain 2x2 are square. Smaller 1x1 sprites stay smaller than 2x2 beds, keeping a consistent world scale.
EXACT row-major order:
Row 1: double bed 2x2, oak frame, headboard at north, two ivory pillows and muted teal blanket, foot south; brick-red upholstered sofa 2x1 with its back at north and open seat facing south; oak kitchen table 2x1 with two simple plates, no chairs; dark oak pub table 2x1 with two tiny beer glasses, no chairs.
Row 2: park bench 2x1 with warm wooden slats and dark iron ends, back north, seat facing south; police desk 2x1 in muted navy and oak with a paper stack and small desk lamp; clothes rack 2x1 on a dark metal rail with three hanging cream, rust and teal garments; compact round-leaf park tree 1x1 with short brown trunk and layered olive-green canopy.
Row 3: square 2x2 stone plaza fountain with circular pale stone basin, teal water and one central small bubbling jet; oak two-door wardrobe 1x1, this variant faces WEST/LEFT, top and west front visible; cast-iron street lamp 1x1 with warm amber lantern, north-facing variant; open east-west wooden doorway 1x1 with masonry jambs and open clear passage.
Row 4: open north-south wooden doorway 1x1 with matching masonry jambs and open clear passage; brick-red sofa 2x1, north-facing variant with its back at south and seat open toward north; matching wooden park bench 2x1, north-facing variant, back south; double bed 2x2, north-facing variant, headboard and pillows at south, foot north.
Constraints: exactly 16 isolated sprites in a strict 4x4 grid, no people, no buildings, no decorative background, no floor swatches, no text, no watermark. Do not add chairs around tables. Keep each complete sprite safely within its own cell with transparent separation.
prompts.commercial:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent wide-object pixel-art atlas for the Last Tram old-town map.
Primary request: A square transparent PNG atlas containing EXACTLY FIVE sprites, arranged in FOUR HORIZONTAL BANDS. Each band is one quarter of the image height. All space around the five objects is true alpha transparency, no labels, no painted checkerboard, no drawn grid or background. Keep every object wholly within its stated band.
Style: authentic coarse 16-bit pixel art with crisp large square clusters, dark umber outlines, honey oak counters, ivory and warm beige surfaces, muted teal glass, charcoal-blue ironwork, rusty red accents. Shallow overhead orthographic top-down RPG view, tops of objects clearly visible, only a short vertical front edge visible. Not isometric. The objects are wide and low, because their map footprints are just ONE CELL DEEP. Common 16-pixel logical tile scale, zero antialiasing, no decorative ground shadows.
EXACT band order from top to bottom:
BAND 1: ONE pub bar counter centered horizontally, four cells wide and one deep (width:height about 4:1). Dark oak bar top with a few tiny amber glasses and a brass tap, walnut front, customer-facing edge SOUTH/DOWN.
BAND 2: ONE café counter centered horizontally, three cells wide and one deep (3:1). Warm oak with cream top, a small dark espresso machine and two tiny stacked cups. This counter's customer-facing edge is NORTH/UP, because the source map uses rotation 2. Show the same overhead camera, with the front trim at the top edge.
BAND 3: TWO SEPARATE counters side-by-side, clearly separated by transparent space. LEFT: small Späti convenience-shop counter, three cells wide and one deep (3:1), cream-and-teal counter with a tiny cash register and a compact row of colorful bottled goods. RIGHT: Imbiss snack-shop counter, three cells wide and one deep (3:1), stainless steel prep top, muted rust front, compact steel warming tray and a small condiment bottle. Both customer-facing edges SOUTH/DOWN. Each of these is no more than 40% of the total image width.
BAND 4: ONE long tram stop shelter centered horizontally, six cells wide and one deep (6:1). A slim elongated blue-grey steel shelter with flat teal-glass canopy roof seen from above, sparse thin roof supports and a slim warm wooden bench integrated beneath. The shelter must be extremely wide and shallow rather than a tall front elevation, and completely inside the band. No stop sign, no timetable board outside shelter; those are separate game assets.
Layout/scale: Band 1 bar width about half the total image width, band 2 café counter width about three eighths, band 3 two counters each three eighths, band 4 shelter width about three quarters. Objects use consistent world scale rather than all being inflated to equal width. Transparent padding between bands.
Constraints: exactly five objects; do not duplicate them, do not add people or vehicles; no floor, no buildings, no scenery; no words, no readable text, no branding, no watermark.
prompts.walk_player:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: four-direction WALKING ANIMATION sprite sheet for the pixel-art top-down European city game Last Tram.
Primary request: A square transparent PNG sprite sheet containing exactly 16 frames in a strict 4-column x 4-row grid. FOUR frames of a real walk cycle per direction. All frames show the SAME character with identical clothes, hairstyle, proportions, scale and camera. The frames are animation assets, not decorative illustrations or poses.
Style/medium: authentic coarse 16-bit RPG pixel art with chunky visible square pixels, very few colors, strong readable silhouette, crisp hard edges, no smooth illustration, no antialiasing. Shallow overhead orthographic top-down camera, matching an old-town tile-based RPG. Think a modest 16 logical pixel wide, 24 logical pixel tall actor inside a 32x32 logical-pixel frame. Keep the entire character including shoes, centered in every cell, same head height and same foot baseline, plenty of transparent padding. Never overlap another cell. No ground or cast shadows.
Exact grid meaning:
ROW 1: walking SOUTH/DOWN, face visible.
ROW 2: walking WEST/LEFT, left-facing profile.
ROW 3: walking NORTH/UP, character's BACK visible, NO face.
ROW 4: walking EAST/RIGHT, right-facing profile.
In EVERY row, columns 1 through 4 are these four consecutive animation phases:
1) left-leg contact, left foot reaching forward, right foot back, opposite arm swing;
2) passing pose, feet near center, right knee lifting, arms near center;
3) right-leg contact, right foot reaching forward, left foot back, opposite arm swing;
4) passing pose, feet near center, left knee lifting, arms near center.
The fourth frame flows smoothly back into the first. Show visibly DIFFERENT leg/foot positions in each successive frame. Keep head and torso positions steady without horizontal drifting. Side views must alternate a leading extended foot and a passing upright stance, not four copies of one pose. North-facing frames show hair/back of head and back of the outfit. Facing direction is constant within each row.
Background: REAL alpha transparency, no painted checkerboard, no floor patches.
Constraints: exactly four rows and four columns, one full-body actor per cell, no labels, no words, no watermark, no extra people or objects, no motion blur.
Character identity: Young adult traveler, light warm skin, short chestnut hair, long dark navy-blue jacket over a muted teal scarf, charcoal-blue trousers, warm brown shoes, small muted rust satchel on the character's anatomical left side. Restrained urban clothing. Keep the satchel on the same anatomical side as the character turns.
